_note: Hand-translated English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 1 (verses 2-22; v.1 absent from Cairo source). Drafted as a high-fidelity exemplar for the cached translation prompt — matching the Bereshit 1 / 22 / 41 voice. Saadia-specific moves preserved: v.5 צלב = 'loins' (for ירך); v.6 וסאיר = 'and the rest of'; v.7 את'מרו וסעו = 'bore fruit and spread out' (note Saadia takes ישרצו as 'spreading' not 'swarming'); v.7 גדא גדא repeated intensifier; v.8 ישאהד = 'see/witness' (for ידע); v.9 לקומה = 'to his people'; v.10 נחתאל = 'let us scheme'; v.10 ויכון אד'א = 'and it shall be when'; v.10 יהרבונא = 'and drive us out' (causative interpretation of ועלה מן הארץ); v.11 ולאה' ד'מה = 'guards of tribute' (for שרי מסים); v.11 קרא מכ'אזין = 'fortified storehouse-towns' (for ערי מסכנות); v.11 אלפיום=פתום (Saadia identifies Pithom with Faiyum) and עין שמס=רעמסס (Ein Shams=Raamses, per gloss table); v.12 צ'גרו = 'dreaded' (for ויקצו); v.13 ואסתכ'דם = 'pressed into service'; v.13/14 באקמא = 'with cruelty' (for בפרך); v.14 אעמאל אלצחרא = 'labors of the open country' (Saadia takes שדה as open desert/wilderness); v.15 אלקואבל = 'the midwives'; v.16 אלמת'בר = 'the birth-stool' (for אבנים); v.18 מא באלכן = 'what is your concern' (for מדוע); v.19 בציראת = 'skilled / quick' (Saadia interprets חיות as expert women, not 'lively/animal'); v.21 חגבהן = 'sheltered them' (Saadia's interpretive gloss on the houses: protection from Pharaoh); v.22 גמיע קואדה = 'all his officers' (Saadia narrows לכל-עמו to 'commanders' — the order is military); v.22 באלניל = 'into the Nile' (יאר → Saadia's place identification = the Nile).

translations.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
translations.5: And the sum of the souls — those issuing from the loins of Jacob — was seventy souls, together with Joseph, who was in Egypt.
translations.6: And Joseph died, and all his brothers, and the rest of the people of that generation.
translations.7: And the sons of Israel bore fruit, and spread out, and multiplied, and grew strong — very, very — until that land was filled with them.
translations.8: And a new king arose over Egypt, who had not seen Joseph.
translations.9: And he said to his people: 'Behold, the people of the sons of Israel — they are more numerous and stronger than us.
translations.10: Come, let us scheme against them, so that they shall not multiply; and it shall be, when war comes upon us, that they too will join with our enemies, and they shall war against us, and shall drive us out from the land.'
translations.11: And they appointed over them guards of tribute, so as to torment them with their burdens; and they built fortified storehouse-towns for Pharaoh — in al-Faiyum (Pithom) and in Ein Shams (Raamses).
translations.12: And as much as they tormented them, so they multiplied and prospered — until [the Egyptians] were filled with dread before the sons of Israel.
translations.13: And the Egyptians pressed the sons of Israel into service with cruelty.
translations.14: And they made their lives bitter with hard labor — with mortar and brick, and with all the labors of the open country; all their service which they pressed them into with cruelty.
translations.15: And the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives — the name of one of whom was Shiphrah, and the other Puah —
translations.16: He said: 'When you deliver the Hebrew women, look upon the birth-stool: if it be a son, then kill him; and if it be a daughter, then let her live.'
translations.17: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt had told them; and they let the boys live.
translations.18: And the king of Egypt called for them, and said to them: 'What is your concern that you have done this thing, and have let the boys live?'
translations.19: They said to him: 'It is because — unlike the Egyptian women — the Hebrew women are skilled; before the midwife comes in to them, they have given birth.'
translations.20: And God dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied, and grew very strong.
translations.21: And when the midwives feared God, He made for them houses where they would be sheltered.
translations.22: And Pharaoh commanded all his officers, saying: 'Every son that is born to them — throw him into the Nile; and every daughter — let her live.'
